title: A Letter for the Portrait
premise: Coral Ishikawa, a night-shift taxi dispatcher with an uncanny ear for lies, has quietly cracked three 'accidental' deaths the police misfiled — the last belonging to her mentor, retired judge Amara Voss. A confession letter arrives postmarked the day after Amara's funeral, unsigned, referencing a fourth death: Coral's own mother, whose drowning twenty years ago was ruled an accident and sealed shut by everyone in the river town of Halcyon Bend. As Coral and her found family — dispatcher Marisol, retired cop Teddy Okafor, and Amara's estranged grandson Dev — dig into the sealed case, they find Amara herself helped bury the truth to protect the town's most powerful family, the Ashcombes, whose patriarch is hosting an anniversary dinner where the truth will finally surface. Coral must choose between exposing a dead mentor's complicity and letting a killer walk, and at the dinner she forces a confession that rewrites her mother's death — and her own memory of it.
about_author: Rosalind Vasquez spent a decade answering phones for a livery service in a fading port town before turning to fiction, and she still swears she can hear a lie through a landline. She lives with her partner and a one-eyed cat named Verdict, and writes only after midnight.
